title: Volume of a Rectangular Prism
short: V = l × w × h counts layers of cubes.
trouble: Children add the three dimensions, or report volume in square units.

blocks.html: You can find volume by counting unit cubes in layers. For a rectangular prism (a box shape), the counting turns into a formula.
$V = l \times w \times h$: length times width gives the cubes in one layer, and times the height counts the layers. Volume is measured in cubic units, such as cubic centimeters ($\text{cm}^{3}$).

A box 5 cm long and 3 cm wide holds 5 rows of 3 one-centimeter cubes in its bottom layer: $5 \times 3 = 15$. If it is 4 cm high, there are 4 layers: $15 \times 4 = 60$ cubes. Each cube is 1 cubic centimeter, so the volume is 60 cubic centimeters.

blocks.cap: Change the length, width and height with the sliders and watch $l \times w \times h$.

blocks.title: A box
blocks.q: Find the volume of a box 5 cm long, 3 cm wide and 4 cm high.

blocks.title: A cube
blocks.q: A cube has edges 6 inches long. What is its volume?

blocks.html: Adding the three edges ($5 + 3 + 4 = 12$) or writing square units. Adding edges does not count cubes, and square units measure flat area. Check: picture the cubes in one layer, then count the layers.
